3  JUDGMENT MFA No.20964/2011 is filed by the Insurance Company challenging the judgment and award dated 17.06.2010 passed by the Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal & Fast Track Court-I, Koppal,
in MVC No.244/2008 questioning the liability fastened on it to pay compensation, whereas MFA No.21881/2011 is filed by the claimant for seeking enhancement of compensation.
2.

Brief facts of the case are that respondent No.2-Goneppa is the owner of the tractor-trailer bearing registration No.KA-37/T-7847 - 7848 and the claimant was working as a workman in the said tractor under the employment of respondent No.2.
Respondent No.2-owner of the tractor had given the tractor on hire basis to respondent No.3.

On 23.11.2006 when the claimant was going on the tractor trailer to unload the electric poles and wires on Koppala Kushtagi road, the driver of the said tractor was driving the said tractor-trailer with high speed and in rash and negligent manner and due to which the claimant fell down from the trolley and caused injury to NC:
2023:KHC-D:10656 the claimant and therefore, the claimant has filed the claim petition under Section 166 of the M.V. Act and the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.1,22,800/- with interest at the rate of 8% holding the Insurance Company shall indemnify the owner of tractor-trailer and to pay compensation.
3. Head the arguments and perused the records.
4. Being aggrieved by the liability fastened on the Insurance Company, the present appeal is filed.

The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the tractor-trailer was given hire basis by respondent No.2- owner to respondent No.3-company and respondent No.3- compnay has used said tractor for transportation of electric poles and wires and claimant was engaged as a workman while transportation of the same.
Therefore, submitted that the tractor was given on hire basis.
Hence, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify the owner of the tractor.
Therefore, fastened liability on the insurance company is not correct.
Therefore, prays for exoneration insurance company from the liability.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the claimants and owner and contractor have justified the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
6. Ex.P.1 and P.2 are FIR and complaint in which it is stated the allegation regarding factum of accident that the claimant was travelled in the said tractor-trailer as a workman.
It is further stated that respondent No.2- Goneppa is the owner of the tractor and respondent No.3 is the construction company has taken the said tractor trailer on hire basis from respondent No.2.
Therefore, it is proved that the tractor-trailer was used on hire basis.
Ex.R.1-Insurance Policy which prohibits giving the tractor on hire basis and if the vehicle is used on hire and contract basis then the insurance company is not liable.

The claimant while giving evidence has stated that he was under Abdul Rehaman S/O. Nabisab vs The Divisional Manager on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23023100/
4 the employment of respondent No.2-Goneppa in his tractor as above stated and the said tractor was given on contract basis to respondent no.3 for transportation of electric poles and wires and while travelling so met with the accident.

sentences.text: Therefore, all the evidence proved that NC: 2023:KHC-D:10656 respondent No.2 being owner of the tractor-trailer has given tractor-trailer on hire basis to respondent No.3 and the claimant has travelled in the trolley which was given on hire basis.
Therefore, the appellant-insurance company has successfully established its defence as per Sub-Section (2) of 149 of the M.V. Act.
Therefore, it is liable to be exonerated and it is not liable to indemnify respondent No.2-owner of the tractor-trailer.

7. Therefore, when it is proved that respondent No.2 is the owner of tractor-trailer has given the said vehicle on hire and contract basis to respondent No.3- construction company as above stated since there is violation of conditions of insurance policy, the insurance company is liable to be exonerated.
Therefore, respondent No.2 being owner of tractor and respondent No.3-company being the contractee who has taken tractor-trailer on hire basis are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Respondent No.2 being owner of the tractor-trailer was not supposed to give the tractor-trailer on hire basis and respondent No.3 being company was not supposed to NC:
2023:KHC-D:10656 receive the tractor-trailer on hire basis.
Therefore, both respondent Nos.2 and 3 have violated the conditions of insurance policy.
Therefore, in this regard respondent Nos.2 and 3 being owner and contractor are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Therefore, both are equally liable to pay compensation to the claimant.

8. However, as per Sub-Section (2) of 149 of the MV Act the insurance company is successful in establishing its defence but as per Section (1) (5) (7) of 149 of the MV Act the insurance company as if judgment debtor shall satisfy the claim to the claimant and then recover the said amount from respondent Nos.2 and 3.

As per Sub-Section (1) of Section 149 of the MV Act whoever risk is covered as per Section 147 then even though insurance company is liable to avoid the liability but as if judgment debtor shall satisfy the claim to the claimants then recover from respondent No.2-owner of the tractor and respondent No.3-contractor.
Since the claimant is proved to be travelling along with goods in the tractor-trailer being authorized representative of owner.

Therefore, the risk NC:
2023:KHC-D:10656 such person is covered under Section 147 of the MV Act.
Therefore, an order of pay and recovery is made as per (1) (5) (7) Section 149 of the MV Act.
Therefore, the risk of the claimant is proved to be covered under Section 147 of the MV Act.

Therefore, the insurance company shall pay compensation at the first instance to the claimant, then recover it from respondent Nos.2 and 3, also in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of the Pappu and Others vs. Vinod Kumar Lamba and Another1; National Insurance Company Limited vs. Swaran Singh and Others 2 and also as per the full bench decision of this Court in the case of New India Assurance Company Limited vs. Yellavva and Another3.

sentences.text: REGARDING QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION:
10. In the present case, from the medical evidence on record it is proved that the claimant had suffered fracture of lower end of tibia bone.
Muscles exposed in the under lying left foot, CLW over dorsum of left foot and injury to left foot and ankle and other injuries.

11. The tribunal awarded the compensation under various heads as under:
 Sl. Heads. Amount in  No. (Rs.)
 1. Towards pain and suffering.

40,000  2. Towards loss of amenities 15,000  3. Towards loss of income during 9,000  rest period  4. Towards loss of future income 28,800  5. Towards medical expenses 25,000  6. Towards miscellaneous expenses 5,000  Total: 1,22,800  - 11 -  NC: 2023:KHC-D:10656 12.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained, a compensation of Rs.70,000/- is awarded towards pain and suffering.
Further, a compensation of Rs.50,000/- is awarded towards loss of amenities.
13. The doctor has stated that the claimant had suffered 22% of physical disability towards left leg.
Therefore, considering the evidence of the doctor, 10% functional disability is taken into consideration.
The accident is caused in the year 2006.
Therefore, notional income of Rs.3,750/- per month is taken into consideration, which is recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
The claimant was aged 28 years at the time of accident.
Therefore appropriate applicable multiplier is 17.
Hence, loss of future income due to disability is hereby reassessed and quantified as Rs.76,500/- (Rs.3,750 x 10% x 12 x 17).
14. The compensation awarded towards medical expenses and hospital charges of Rs.25,000/- is as per the actual bills and receipts produced.
Therefore, the same is kept intact.

along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the petition till realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
